title: Statue of Liberty dedicated

when.label: 28 October 1886
when.note: Date of the dedication by President Grover Cleveland. Work on the statue began in France in 1875.

summary: A gift from the people of France, the copper statue designed by Frédéric-Auguste Bartholdi was dedicated at the entrance to New York Harbor in 1886.
description: The French historian Édouard de Laboulaye proposed the statue in 1865 as a monument to friendship between the peoples of France and the United States. Funded by contributions from the French public, it was built in France from 1875 under the sculptor Frédéric-Auguste Bartholdi.

The statue's copper sheets were hammered into shape by hand and assembled over a framework of four giant steel supports designed by Eugène-Emmanuel Viollet-le-Duc and Gustave Eiffel. It was presented in Paris on 4 July 1884, shipped to New York in 1885, and mounted on a pedestal designed by Richard Morris Hunt inside the walls of Fort Wood on Bedloe's Island. President Grover Cleveland dedicated it on 28 October 1886.
context: The statue holds a tablet bearing the date of the Declaration of Independence, 4 July 1776, and was a gift marking the centenary of American independence. It has welcomed millions of immigrants arriving by sea, and it was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1984.

facts.text: Laboulaye proposed the statue in 1865; work began in France in 1875 under Bartholdi.
The supporting framework was designed by Viollet-le-Duc and Eiffel; the pedestal by Richard Morris Hunt.
President Grover Cleveland dedicated the statue on 28 October 1886.
